text: I started having trouble walking recently, and people say I look drunk when I walk. I also feel clumsy in my arms and legs, especially on the right side.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that description; the unilateral clumsiness on the right side is a key detail. To further localize the lesion, do you experience any double vision, facial droop, or arm weakness when you try to lift your right arm? REQUEST IMAGES: MRI_Brain

speaker: Patient
text: I have Crohn disease and it has been difficult to control. I have been taking natalizumab for about a year.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Progressive Multifocal Leukoencephalopathy (PML) secondary to natalizumab therapy. Given your history of Crohn's disease and treatment with natalizumab, combined with progressive unilateral ataxia and gait disturbances, this is highly suspicious for JC virus reactivation in the white matter. We must confirm this immediately with an MRI showing characteristic white matter lesions, but clinically, stopping natalizumab and considering alternative immunomodulators for your Crohn's is the priority to prevent further neurological decline.
